title: Opening 8-bit 'Pizzeria Simulator' fake-out
claim: FFPS opens as an 8-bit tycoon minigame in which the player, as Freddy, throws pizzas to children; a grey-scaled Freddy appears on round 3 and on round 4 the game glitches out and cuts to the Scrap Baby salvage scene.

when.label: During FFPS (the franchisee's Monday–Saturday work week)
when.basis: FFPS presents a six-day work week at the newly re-branded pizzeria; no year is given in-game

notes: The grey Freddy is identified with Shadow Freddy only by fans/wiki; the game gives it no name.

title: Intro tape: checking outside every shift, Paragraph 4
claim: The Cassette Man's opening tape (played over Scrap Baby's salvage) says the listener has been checking outside after every shift as instructed and has found something meeting the criteria of their 'special obligations under Paragraph 4'.
location: Opening cutscene – Scrap Baby salvage tape

when.label: During FFPS (the franchisee's Monday–Saturday work week)
when.basis: FFPS presents a six-day work week at the newly re-branded pizzeria; no year is given in-game

quote: If you are playing this tape, that means that not only have you been checking outside at the end of every shift, as you were instructed to do, but also that you have found something …

title: Intro tape: seal the room and never return
claim: The opening tape instructs the listener to document response times, secure the space, and never return after sealing the room.
location: Opening cutscene – Scrap Baby salvage tape

when.label: During FFPS (the franchisee's Monday–Saturday work week)
when.basis: FFPS presents a six-day work week at the newly re-branded pizzeria; no year is given in-game

quote: Follow these instructions: document response times, then safely secure the space before leaving. Upon sealing the room, you are not to return.

title: Player becomes a Fazbear Entertainment franchisee
claim: Tutorial Unit's intro presents the player as a new Fazbear Entertainment franchisee who has invested their life savings in a franchise package (a small room, some tables, electricity).

when.label: During FFPS (the franchisee's Monday–Saturday work week)
when.basis: FFPS presents a six-day work week at the newly re-branded pizzeria; no year is given in-game

quote: We're talking about becoming a Fazbear Entertainment franchisee. That's right, restaurant ownership and management.

title: 'Newly re-branded Freddy Fazbear's Pizza' and liability disclaimer
claim: The intro calls the business 'the newly re-branded Freddy Fazbear's Pizza' and ends with a disclaimer that Fazbear Entertainment is not responsible for disappearance, death, or dismemberment.

when.label: During FFPS (the franchisee's Monday–Saturday work week)
when.basis: FFPS presents a six-day work week at the newly re-branded pizzeria; no year is given in-game

quote: You are now the face of the newly re-branded Freddy Fazbear's Pizza. Wear that smile with pride and let's make some money. Fazbear Entertainment is not responsible for disappearance, death, or dismemberment.

title: Something outside has been trying to get in for months
claim: In the Liability section, Tutorial Unit warns that discounted items may have something hiding inside, which would only matter if something outside had been trying to get in for months, 'which we are not confirming to be the case'.

when.label: During FFPS (the franchisee's Monday–Saturday work week)
when.basis: FFPS presents a six-day work week at the newly re-branded pizzeria; no year is given in-game

quote: Of course, that would only be a serious danger if there were something outside that's been trying to get in for months now, which we are not confirming to be the case.
notes: Mechanically, poor-condition catalog items can contain an unsalvaged animatronic that then becomes active (see Maintenance Checklist wiki page).

title: Saturday is a big party and the 'ultimate test'
claim: After the first shift Tutorial Unit says there is a big party at the pizzeria on Saturday and calls that day the player's ultimate test.

when.basis: FFPS presents a six-day work week at the newly re-branded pizzeria; no year is given in-game

quote: There's a big party here Saturday, and you should view that day as your ultimate test.

when.label: During FFPS (the franchisee's Monday–Saturday work week)

title: Animatronics are often found in the alley outside the back door
claim: The Cassette Man's first salvage tape says animatronics are found 'quite often' in the alley outside the back door and that 'we aren't sure why'; keeping one risks death.

when.label: During FFPS (the franchisee's Monday–Saturday work week)

title: Salvage tape: 'we are unsure of its origins'
claim: Each later salvage tape describes the animatronic as found in the back alley with unknown origins, offering the choice to complete the Maintenance Checklist or throw it back.

when.label: During FFPS (the franchisee's Monday–Saturday work week)

title: Four salvageable animatronics, in order
claim: The four animatronics offered for salvage are Molten Freddy, Scraptrap, Scrap Baby and Lefty, in that order across the nights; salvaging (or otherwise letting in) all four is required for the Completion ending.

when.label: During FFPS (the franchisee's Monday–Saturday work week)

title: Bad ending: fired for not meeting Paragraph Four
claim: If any salvage animatronic was thrown away, the Cassette Man tells the player they did not meet their special obligations under Paragraph Four and their employment is terminated.

when.label: End of FFPS (after Saturday's shift)
when.basis: Plays after the final (Saturday) shift; no year given

quote: Congratulations on completing the week. Unfortunately, you did not meet your special obligations under Paragraph Four. Your employment is terminated. We’ll mail you your things. End tape.

title: Credits name the tape speaker only 'Cassette Man'
claim: FFPS's cast credits list Dave Steele as 'Cassette Man'. The name 'Henry' is never spoken or printed in FFPS dialogue or credits.

when.label: End of FFPS (after Saturday's shift)
when.basis: Plays after the final (Saturday) shift; no year given

quote: Dave Steele - Cassette Man
notes: 'Henry' comes from the novels and from voice actor PJ Heywood's remark on The FNaF Show, not from game text. See ffps-hry223-label for the only possible in-game hint.

notes: UNVERIFIED LOCATION: the wiki says the tape 'is called HRY223' without saying whether this is on-screen text or an internal file name. Reading 'HRY' as 'Henry' is an inference. Treat this as a weak lead only.

title: Credits: Scraptrap's voice is credited as 'William Afton'
claim: FFPS's cast credits list PJ Heywood as 'William Afton'. PJ Heywood voices the salvaged Springtrap-like animatronic (Scraptrap) in FFPS, so the game's own credits name that character William Afton.

when.label: End of FFPS (after Saturday's shift)
when.basis: Plays after the final (Saturday) shift; no year given

quote: PJ Heywood - William Afton
notes: Cast list per wiki transcript: Heather Masters - Scrap Baby; PJ Heywood - William Afton; Kellen Goff - Molten Freddy; Andy Field - Tutorial Unit; Dave Steele - Cassette Man. The name 'Scraptrap' is not used in FFPS.

title: Lefty blueprint: L.ure E.ncapsulate F.use T.ransport & E.xtract
claim: An Insanity-ending blueprint of Lefty spells out 'L.ure E.ncapsulate F.use T.ransport & E.xtract', lists a False Sensory Output that emits a bracelet code for a 'security receiver', and a 'Dream Wand'/Soother that uses 'lullaby index 01'. It is marked Fazbear Entertainment, Inc.

when.label: During FFPS (the franchisee's Monday–Saturday work week)

notes: Transcribed from the blueprint image. The Puppet is not named; the bracelet/security-receiver and lullaby details echo the Security Puppet and the Puppet's music box.

title: RASC blueprint: simulated presence at body temperature
claim: An Insanity-ending blueprint 'R.emote A.ctivated S.imulated C.' has navigational sensors, a heat uplink/sensor override with 'Variable Alpha to remain at 98.6', and an individual emitter that must stay connected to a central server 'or risk inaccurate represented population'. Marked Fazbear Entertainment, Inc.

when.label: During FFPS (the franchisee's Monday–Saturday work week)
when.basis: FFPS presents a six-day work week at the newly re-branded pizzeria; no year is given in-game

quote: B: Heat Uplink/ Sensor Override. NOTES: Must remain connected to central server at all times or risk duplicate signature. Variable Alpha to remain at 98.6. C: Individual Emitter. …
notes: 98.6 is normal human body temperature in °F. The 'C.' is not expanded. That RASC simulates children to lure the animatronics is an inference, supported by Henry's line about 'chasing the cries of children in some unseen chamber'.

title: SCUP blueprint (Afton Robotics): Remnant injector and reservoir
claim: An Insanity-ending blueprint 'S.calable C.reation of U.lterior P.resence', marked Afton Robotics, LLC, shows an excavating arm, a 'Remnant Injector' and a 'Remnant Reservoir'. It notes the substance must be kept heated and that 'overheating might neutralize the effects permanently'.

when.label: During FFPS (the franchisee's Monday–Saturday work week)
when.basis: FFPS presents a six-day work week at the newly re-branded pizzeria; no year is given in-game

quote: B: Remnant Injector. NOTES: Leave trace line amount on interior. Over-usage/ Over-exposure negates effect. ... D: Remnant Reservoir. NOTES: When heated, no observable motion. Keep in heated tank at sustained temperature. ... …
notes: First in-game use of the word 'Remnant' in the core series. The Scooper is also Sister Location's scooping machine (Circus Baby's UCN line mentions 'the Scooping Room').

title: UCN's roster includes all four FFPS salvage animatronics
claim: UCN's roster of 50 selectable characters (plus Dee Dee's secret extras) includes Molten Freddy, Scrap Baby, Afton and Lefty alongside characters from FNaF1–4, Sister Location and FFPS.

title: UCN never names the player, but many lines accuse them of a killing
claim: UCN's player is never named, and no line says 'William', 'Afton', 'Michael' or 'Henry'. Several characters say the player killed someone ('the one you should not have killed') and cannot die ('a victim that can't perish'; 'You won't die, but you'll wish you could').

notes: The theory that the player is William Afton in a personal hell is not stated anywhere in UCN; it rests on these lines together with FFPS's ending. The roster label 'Afton' refers to an attacking animatronic, not the player.

title: Phone Guy appears as a caller to be muted
claim: Phone Guy is a UCN roster 'character' represented only by incoming calls, which the player must mute quickly or be distracted by noise.
